conventions.convention: The RN model is R_v × (0,∞)_r × S², with signature (-+++), outward sphere orientation, product orientation dv∧dr∧ω, and length-valued v, r, M, q_e and q_m. The excluded center is not supplied with a source.
RN future orientation is selected by N=∂v+(f/2−1)∂r; ℓ=−∂r and n=∂v+(f/2)∂r are future null. The static interior orientation ∂r at fixed t is opposite to this selected orientation when f<0.

The KN model uses the full sphere form β=X dY−Y dX, r>0, Σ=r²+a²Z²>0, and future timelike field N=∂v−(1+f₀²)∂r/2. Its smooth metric extension is established directly; field-equation continuation is conditional on the current KN verification draft.
Signed surface gravity satisfies the ambient covector equation d(g(ξ,ξ))=−2κξ♭. The specified generators give positive outer and negative inner simple-root values, and zero at a double root.
The simple-root RN construction uses dimensionless U,V, an auxiliary length ℓ*>0, UV=−K(r), K′(r₊)=1/ℓ*, and V=e^(κv)>0 on the original ingoing overlap. It supplies no extremal bifurcation chart.

RN fluxes use outward sphere orientation and spacetime orientation dt∧dr∧ω: magnetic flux is 4πq_m and electric dual flux is 4πq_e. Potentials are smooth real one-forms; no circle-bundle normalization or quantization is assumed.

Escape requires one continuous future causal path with finite C¹ subdivisions on each compact parameter interval and nonzero one-sided causal tangents, reaching arbitrarily large r. Its boundary is relative to the selected product model, without conformal infinity.
The ergoregion and stationary-limit set refer specifically to T=∂v; only positive algebraic stationary-limit roots belong to the model. The rotation field is Ψ=X∂Y−Y∂X.

The charged-ring obstruction assumes q≠0 and a specified approach with Σ→0 in the Boyer–Lindquist domain. It obstructs C² nondegenerate metric extension along that approach, conditional on the current Ricci-invariant identity; it supplies no vacuum Kerr obstruction.
Countable Choice is inherited through the geometric, tetrad and intrinsic-area suppliers; the collar proof makes no additional full-choice or dependent-choice assumption.

load_bearing.statement: For real length parameters M,q_e,q_m, the selected model on R_v × (0,∞)_r × S² has g=−f dv²+2 dv dr+r²γ and F=−q_e r⁻² dv∧dr+q_mω, with future timelike field N=∂v+(f/2−1)∂r. The metric is nondegenerate and the field smooth for every r>0.

For real M,a,q, the displayed ingoing KN metric and potential define smooth Lorentzian metric and field data on R_v × (0,∞)_r × S², including axes and positive roots of Δ, with the specified future timelike N. Source-free geometric equations continue conditionally on the exact current KN verification draft.

For either specified RN or KN model under its stated positive-root hypotheses, an outer-root collar has temporal function τ=v−r and a finite C≥0 such that dr(Z)≤C|r−r_H|dτ(Z) for every future causal Z; dτ(Z)>0 for nonzero Z, and dr(Z)≤0 on r=r_H.

For M>0 and M²≥a²+q²>0, either positive root r_H has future null Killing generator χ_H=∂v+(a/R_H)Ψ, signed κ_H=(r_H−r_other)/(2R_H), section area 4πR_H and displayed-gauge potential −A_in(χ_H)=qr_H/R_H, where R_H=r_H²+a².

On a nonempty static dyonic RN sphere product with f≠0, the sphere fluxes are 4πq_m and 4πq_e, the displayed north/south potentials are smooth and differentiate to F, and a global smooth real one-form potential exists exactly when q_m=0.

For M>0, Q²>0 and M²≥Q², every positive RN root is a regular crossing. When M²>Q² the simple outer root admits the stated smooth local bifurcation extension. Field-equation continuation is conditional on the current RN verification draft; at extremality only the regular ingoing crossing is asserted.
For M>0, Q²>0 and M²≥Q², the selected ingoing RN escape set is {r>r_H}, where r_H=M+√(M²−Q²), and its relative boundary is {r=r_H}.
For M>0 and M²≥a²+q²>0, the selected ingoing KN escape set is {r>r₊} and its relative boundary is {r=r₊}, including the extremal case.

seams_checked.note: Checked RN/KN data, geometric electrovac, verification, invariant and dyonic-flux interfaces against their consuming claims. Static-domain restrictions and orientations are retained; smooth extension is proved locally. Verification, invariant and KN flux uses explicitly retain draft qualifications.

The horizon, signed surface-gravity, area, selected escape-path and approached-extension uses match the current vocabulary Definition. Relative escape boundaries are kept distinct from conformal event horizons.

RN/KN horizon consumers preserve the supplied parameter ranges, generators, signs, gauges and selected escape observable. The RN consumer separately derives its uncharged branch rather than applying the charged supplier outside Q²>0. The dyonic consumer restricts the explicit RN potential criterion to the nonrotating RN case.

The KN first-law consumer uses the outer-horizon formulas where a²+q²>0. Its separate Schwarzschild lemma derives the excluded a=q=0 slice directly from the unrestricted smooth KN metric extension, preserving the selected orientation and signed surface-gravity convention.
